components.institution_label: Maternity/Parental/Adoption Leave or Primary Caregiver Leave
components.description: Fifty-two weeks of leave for a pregnant employee or any employee who declares in writing to be the primary caregiver of a newborn or adopted child; paid only through the EI supplement (c2), the balance unpaid.
components.mechanism_note: The leave itself; its pay is the separate EI supplement (c2) linked within it (V4; checklist §5 ex. 1). 'The balance of the leave shall be without pay.'
components.faculty_group_note: employees holding an appointment 'that is probationary, with tenure, with continuing status, or without term' (bargaining unit of faculty and librarians, Art. 4.1)
components.eligible_parent_wording: an employee who is pregnant and who declares in writing to be the primary caregiver, or an employee who declares in writing to be the primary care giver of a new born or adopted child
components.caregiver_condition_wording: declares in writing to be the primary caregiver / primary care giver of a new born or adopted child
components.service_requirement: none stated for probationary, tenured, continuing-status or without-term appointments; limited-term appointees: one year of employment preceding the anticipated birth or custody
components.duration_note: Must be taken uninterrupted and completed within 52 weeks of the birth or adoption; may begin up to eight weeks before the birth or custody. Limited-term appointees: 52 weeks or to the end of the appointment, whichever is earlier (not the member's path, U8).
components.time_window: commences within the period from eight weeks before the estimated or actual date of birth or custody to 52 weeks after it; must be completed within 52 weeks of the birth or adoption
components.notice: as much written notice as possible, not less than four weeks except in emergencies, to the Department Head and Dean
components.relief_note: A formal leave of absence with no relief stated (R9).

sequence.note: An employee takes either the primary caregiver leave (21.7.1, with c2 and c6) or the secondary caregiver leave (21.7.2); R15b, R6.

notes: Sources: one usable source, 2018_02 (USFA text copy of the 2014-2017 U of S / USFA collective agreement, continuing year to year under Art. 31.1; the document's version note says it is the governing document on 2018-03-13). The signed scan 2018_01 has no text layer.
Governing document: the collective agreement covers probationary and tenured faculty (Art. 4.1, 13.3); missing is false.

Member's path (U8): an EI-eligible tenure-stream employee receives the 21.7.1.3(i) supplement (c2). Other paths, in notes only: (ii) probationary, tenured, permanent-status or without-term employees found ineligible for EI solely on the insurable-employment test receive 95% of normal salary for up to 35 weeks; (iii) other employees not eligible for EI receive 95% of salary for the first two weeks, the balance unpaid.

The supplement clause describes EI's former two-week waiting period; on the reference date EI's wait is one week (EI Act s. 13; programs.csv). The supplement is coded as its stated 35-week envelope from the start of the leave (V4, R21 Saskatchewan example); EI starts one week after the leave starts.

Primary vs secondary caregiver: the 21.7.1 option (c1 leave, c2 supplement, c6 extension) and the 21.7.2 secondary caregiver leave (c5) are linked in_lieu_of (R15b; caregiver conditions are gender-neutral, R6). EI benefits are granted under either option, but no component is shared by both options (no statutory leave is coded, the agreement does not rely on the SEA leave), so EI is linked to the primary caregiver leave c1.

Chain, birth parent: primary caregiver leave 52 (c1) with the 95% supplement for its first 35 weeks (c2, within c1 from the start); EI maternity 15 from week 2 (c3) -> EI parental 35 (c4); then extension of leave without pay up to 1 year (c6, consecutive_after c1). Alternative: secondary caregiver leave 35, first week paid (c5), in lieu of c1.

Chain, non-birth parent: as primary caregiver, leave 52 (c1) with supplement 35 within it (c2); EI parental 35 from week 2 (c4, concurrent_with c1, offset 1); then extension up to 1 year (c6). Alternative: secondary caregiver leave 35, first week paid (c5), in lieu of c1.

Benefit coverage: during the paid portion both parties pay their shares; during the unpaid portion the Employer maintains group life, LTD, extended health and dental coverage (21.7.1.4.1-2). Sabbatical: up to one year of each parental leave counts as qualifying service (21.7.1.10, 20.5.2). A career development increase is earned for the first year of the parental leave (18.7.7). These are not components.

Art. 10.1 incorporates into the agreement all rights conferred by federal, provincial or municipal laws, without naming a statute; not treated as reliance on the Saskatchewan Employment Act's leave sections (U4). The statutory floor is filled from statutory_baseline.csv (U7).

Documents cited but not saved: the Academic Long Term Disability Plan document (Salary Continuation Plan, 22.5; flagged on c11, c12); the Faculty Information Handbook, 1973 (5.1, past terms maintained unless altered); the Compulsory Group Life Insurance, Voluntary Group Life, Pension, Dental and Extended Health plan documents (22.2-22.16); the University Calendar (term dates); unit Guidelines for Assignment of Duties (11.5); the EAP Joint Stakeholder Agreement (22.19); Guidelines for Starting Salary Recommendations (18.2.6); Guidelines for the Preparation of a Standardized CV (12.11.1); Board of Governors 1997 search policy (MOA 2).
Calendar: the academic year has three terms T1-T3 (Definitions, 11.2.1), with no length in weeks and not called semesters or quarters; no calendar entry (R8). No component is stated in terms.

Not components: political, court, educational, administrative and sabbatical leaves, leave with pay to work away (21.5), the reduced appointment retirement plan (24.5) and the child and elder care research committee (MOA 4): none can be taken for a birth or adoption, or none gives time off, pay or protection to a new parent.
